_comment: **The one list of what the pipeline will read, and it is data rather than code on purpose.**
It lived in two places before this: a set in ingest.py and a duplicate tuple in
fixtures/generate_corpus.py. The corpus generator's coverage report compared the corpus against the
duplicate, so its denominator was the list itself: it could confirm that two copies of one list agreed,
and it reported '15/15 formats covered (complete)' while a third of what the parser reads was
unreachable. Nothing was wrong with any individual format. The measurement could not see the gap.
'accepted' is what the worker picks up. 'excluded' is what the parser advertises and the pipeline
deliberately will not read, and **every entry carries a reason and how it was decided**: tested, or
unverified. An exclusion without a reason is indistinguishable from the oversight this file exists to
prevent, which is exactly how a client's scanned TIFF stayed invisible.
Checked against docs/parser-formats.json, which scripts/dump_parser_formats.py generates from the
parser image, by tests/test_format_coverage.py. **A parser upgrade that adds a format fails that test
until somebody decides here**, which is the control that was missing.
_corpus_comment: **The difference between 'the worker reads sixty formats' and 'the corpus must show twenty-one of them'.**
The coverage report used to compare the corpus against the whole accepted list, which was both circular
and unhelpful: with fifty-six accepted suffixes it would have reported 15/56 and read as a failing corpus
rather than as a list that had grown to include a long tail no client hands over. What the corpus has to
prove is the formats a small business actually brings: its word processor files, its spreadsheets, its
scans, its saved emails and web pages.
Everything here has a business reason. The rest of the accepted list is a long tail that costs nothing to
support and does not need a fixture each.

excluded..aac: REFUSED PENDING A DECISION: the parser advertises audio and transcribes it, and this image has no ASR model installed -- transformers is present but no whisper weights are, so a transcription attempt fails. Accepting these means promising that a client's meeting recording becomes searchable, which needs the model added to the parser image first and is a size and CPU decision rather than a one-line one.
excluded..afp: UNVERIFIED. IBM Advanced Function Presentation, advertised as AFP. A mainframe print stream that needs a renderer; no sample was available and it is unlikely in the target market.
excluded..avi: REFUSED PENDING A DECISION: video, no ASR model installed. See .aac.
excluded..boxnote: UNVERIFIED. Box Notes, advertised as BOXNOTE. No sample was available and it is not a format a small business is likely to hold directly.
excluded..dclx: BY DESIGN: docling's own interchange format rather than something a client produces. Accepting it would promise ingestion for a file type that exists only inside the tool.
excluded..ebc: TESTED 2026-10-16: the parser fails on an EBCDIC-encoded text file. Advertising it and refusing it are the same outcome for a client, so it is refused here where the reason can be stated.
excluded..ebcdic: TESTED 2026-10-16: same as .ebc, the parser fails on it.
excluded..flac: REFUSED PENDING A DECISION: audio, no ASR model installed. See .aac.
excluded..gz: BY DESIGN: an archive rather than a document, and the compound spelling matters. A path ending .tar.gz has the suffix .gz -- the worker matches the last component -- so excluding '.tar.gz' would leave '.gz' unaccounted for and a compressed file would be silently dropped. The parser advertises '.tar.gz' as METS_GBS, an archival package format, and neither it nor a bare .gz is something a client expects to find in search results.
excluded..json: BY DESIGN: docling's own serialisation of a parsed document. A client's .json is data rather than a document, and the parser would read it as a docling document or refuse it.
excluded..key: UNVERIFIED. Apple Keynote, advertised as IWORK_KEYNOTE. No sample was available.
excluded..m4a: REFUSED PENDING A DECISION: audio, no ASR model installed. See .aac.
excluded..mkv: REFUSED PENDING A DECISION: video, no ASR model installed. See .aac.
excluded..mov: REFUSED PENDING A DECISION: video, no ASR model installed. See .aac. A phone records video by default, so this is the commonest way a small business produces a recording.
excluded..mp3: REFUSED PENDING A DECISION: audio, no ASR model installed. See .aac. Voicemail and meeting recordings are ordinary small-business documents, so this gap is worth closing deliberately rather than by accident.
excluded..mp4: REFUSED PENDING A DECISION: video, no ASR model installed. See .aac.
excluded..msg: UNVERIFIED. The parser advertises it alongside .eml under EMAIL, and an Outlook saved message is common in a small business, but a real .msg is an OLE2 compound file rather than RFC 822 and no sample was available to test. The corpus has none and one could not be synthesised reliably. **This is the next format to verify**, and it is refused rather than promised because adding a suffix is a claim that files with it are ingested.
excluded..ogg: REFUSED PENDING A DECISION: audio, no ASR model installed. See .aac.
excluded..pages: UNVERIFIED. Apple Pages, advertised by the parser as IWORK_PAGES. No sample was available. Common on a client's Mac, so worth testing rather than assuming.
excluded..wav: REFUSED PENDING A DECISION: audio, no ASR model installed. TESTED 2026-10-16: the parser fails on a WAV.
excluded..webm: REFUSED PENDING A DECISION: video, no ASR model installed. See .aac.
excluded..xml: BY DESIGN: four schemas share this extension -- JATS, USPTO, XBRL and doclang -- and the parser guesses between them. A client's .xml is far more often configuration or a machine export than a document, and a wrong guess surfaces as a parse failure that reads like a corrupt file. The unambiguous variants are accepted (.nxml, .xbrl, .dclg), so only the bare extension is refused. This also covers .dclg.xml, whose suffix is .xml.
